evidence_summary.classification_policy: permeability, EMSA/CD DNA binding, radiolabeled precursor incorporation and SEM/flow-cytometry assays are direct; in vivo LPS protection remains phenotype-supported without direct LPS binding assay

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lfcin4 and Lfcin5 have direct membrane-permeabilizing activity in model vesicles and bacterial cells, with Lfcin4 generally stronger in the reported assays.

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=7:Lfcin4 and Lfcin5 permeabilize model and bacterial membranes

mechanism_claims.limitations: Membrane conclusions are strongest for Lfcin4; Lfcin5 did not support S. aureus inner-membrane permeabilization in the PI assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: PI flow-cytometry supports Lfcin4 inner-membrane damage in S. aureus ATCC25923 and S. enteritidis CVCC3377, while Lfcin5 inner-membrane damage is supported for S. enteritidis but not S. aureus.

source_locators.locator: pdf_text:Permeabilization of the inner membrane in S. aureus and S. enteritidis

mechanism_claims.limitations: This claim preserves the source-negative result for Lfcin5 against the S. aureus inner membrane.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lfcin4 and Lfcin5 directly bind bacterial genomic DNA in gel retardation and DNA circular-dichroism assays; source text reports stronger DNA binding for Lfcin4.

targets: bacterial genomic DNA from E. coli CICC21530

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=8:Lfcin4 and Lfcin5 bind to bacterial genomic DNA

mechanism_claims.limitations: DNA binding is direct in vitro evidence; it does not by itself quantify intracellular target engagement in all tested organisms.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lfcin4 directly inhibits DNA, RNA and protein precursor incorporation in S. aureus ATCC25923; Lfcin5 does not show the same inhibition in the reported assay.

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=9:Lfcin4 inhibits the synthesis of DNA, RNA and protein precursors

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct inhibition is assigned to Lfcin4 only; Lfcin5 is retained as a source-negative/needs-further-study comparator for this endpoint.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lfcin4 and Lfcin5 protect mice in LPS challenge assays and reduce inflammatory pathology markers, but local source evidence supports this as an in vivo anti-endotoxin phenotype rather than a direct LPS-binding mechanism assay.

source_locators.locator: xml:sec=11:Lfcin4 and Lfcin5 protect mice from lethal challenge with LPS

mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not promote this phenotype to direct LPS neutralization/binding mechanism without a direct binding assay in local materials.

overclaim_guardrails: MIC/growth activity was not used as a direct mechanism claim
Lfcin5 S. aureus inner membrane non-support is preserved as a limitation
LPS protection is not promoted to direct LPS-binding mechanism
